questions.questionText:
Statements:
I. Unprecedented torrential rainfall lashed the coastal state for four consecutive days.
II. Low-lying residential colonies were severely inundated and road traffic was brought to a standstill.
options: Both statements I and II are effects of independent causes
Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect
Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect
Both statements I and II are independent causes
questions.hint: Determine which event occurred first chronologically and led naturally to the second event.
questions.explanation: Heavy torrential rainfall directly causes the subsequent flooding and traffic disruption in low-lying localities. Thus, Statement I is the direct cause and Statement II is its effect.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Read both statements and assess chronological precedence.
Step 2: Check for a direct causal mechanism (did Event A trigger Event B?).
Step 3: If no connection exists, check if they stem from independent causes or a common cause.
Step 4: Conclude: Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect.
questions.memoryTip: Ask "Why did this happen?" If one statement directly answers why the other occurred, you have a direct cause-effect pair!

I. The state government announced a flat 50% subsidy on modern drip irrigation equipment for farmers.
II. Thousands of small and marginal farmers submitted applications at district agricultural offices.
options: Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect
Both statements I and II are independent causes
Both statements I and II are effects of independent causes
Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect
questions.hint: Incentives and announcements trigger human behavior and applications.
questions.explanation: The government subsidy announcement provided the direct economic incentive that motivated farmers to apply. Statement I is the cause and Statement II is the resulting effect.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Read both statements and assess chronological precedence.
Step 2: Check for a direct causal mechanism (did Event A trigger Event B?).
Step 3: If no connection exists, check if they stem from independent causes or a common cause.
Step 4: Conclude: Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect.
questions.memoryTip: Ask "Why did this happen?" If one statement directly answers why the other occurred, you have a direct cause-effect pair!

questions.questionText:

I. The central petroleum ministry slashed import tariffs on crude oil by 40%.
II. Domestic fuel retailers reduced the retail prices of petrol and diesel across the country.
options: Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect
Both statements I and II are effects of independent causes
Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect
Both statements I and II are independent causes
questions.hint: Tariff reductions lead to retail price reductions in regulated sectors.
questions.explanation: A reduction in import tariffs reduces the procurement cost of crude oil, which directly enables fuel retailers to pass on price cuts to consumers. Statement I is cause, II is effect.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Read both statements and assess chronological precedence.
Step 2: Check for a direct causal mechanism (did Event A trigger Event B?).
Step 3: If no connection exists, check if they stem from independent causes or a common cause.
Step 4: Conclude: Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect.
questions.memoryTip: Ask "Why did this happen?" If one statement directly answers why the other occurred, you have a direct cause-effect pair!

I. Major IT firms across the metropolitan region reported a 25% attrition rate among experienced software architects.
II. Several global technology conglomerates opened new high-paying development centres in the city.
options: Both statements I and II are independent causes
Both statements I and II are effects of independent causes
Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect
questions.hint: Notice the chronological precedence: new employment opportunities induce higher employee turnover.
questions.explanation: The opening of new high-paying tech centres by global firms created lucrative opportunities that caused experienced staff to leave their existing employers. Hence, Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Read both statements and assess chronological precedence.
Step 2: Check for a direct causal mechanism (did Event A trigger Event B?).
Step 3: If no connection exists, check if they stem from independent causes or a common cause.
Step 4: Conclude: Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect.
questions.memoryTip: Ask "Why did this happen?" If one statement directly answers why the other occurred, you have a direct cause-effect pair!
